structured_output.summary: The diff implements String.prototype.repeat in its own file and follows the spec steps in order. RequireObjectCoercible and ToString run before ToIntegerOrInfinity(count). The RangeError for n < 0 or n = +∞ is thrown, and n = 0 returns the empty String. Errors from ? are propagated, and _string_ is rooted across the count conversion. The only addition beyond the spec is an engine length limit (MAX_STRING_LENGTH, 2^29-24 code units) that throws a RangeError rather than returning a value. That limit is a general implementation cap, not keyed on test inputs, and it is permitted because the spec leaves maximum string length to the implementation. The empty-string case is handled correctly even for huge n. No other files changed. The gate report shows 24 new passes and 0 regressions.
structured_output.notes_for_next_attempt: Minor: the comment "The callback-free conversions below may collect garbage" (above with_roots) is inaccurate. ToIntegerOrInfinity(count) can call user valueOf/toString when count is an object, so it is not callback-free. Reword the comment only; the behaviour is correct. The MAX_STRING_LENGTH cap is an engine limit that throws RangeError; keep it, and check that it matches any limit the engine already defines elsewhere.
